analysis: Atherosclerosis is a condition characterized by the buildup of fats, cholesterol, and other substances in and on the artery walls. Homocystinemia (high levels of homocysteine) is known to damage the lining of arteries and promote blood clots, thus predisposing to atherosclerosis. Elevated levels of fibrinogen, a blood clotting factor, are associated with increased risk of atherosclerosis as it can lead to thicker blood and increased clot formation. Lipoprotein(a) is a type of lipoprotein similar to LDL, which is known to contribute to the buildup of plaques in arteries, thus predisposing to atherosclerosis. Calcium, in the context of dietary or serum calcium, does not directly predispose to atherosclerosis; rather, it is the calcification within the atherosclerotic plaques that is often observed in advanced stages of the disease.
